$comment: Legends design tokens: the single source for Tailwind (web/) and Flutter ThemeData (mobile/). Values come from the design system board (legends-ui/Main.dc.html), and since X32 (2026-10-25) Legends' own signature after the owner asked for colours of our own: night ink (bg, panel), emerald (brand) for bands, table heads and the current section, gold for the calls to action and the coach's row, mint rings (ring) and ivory tabs (chrome) instead of the management games' blue and silver. Since X56 (2026-10-29) a day theme too: colorLight overrides the grounds and the text on html.light, and ink darkens the accents' text there. Change here first, then regenerate both.

colorLight.$comment: The day theme (X56, the owner's request 2026-10-29), on html.light: only the colours that change. The ground turns to warm paper and the ink to our night navy; the accents (gold, emerald, red) stay as they are for fills, and their text takes the darker ink below, so a gold word stays readable on paper. The match broadcast stays at night (.theme-night).

ink.$comment: The day theme's text in an accent colour (text-gold, text-success...): the same hue, dark enough for 4.5:1 on paper and on the bar's glass (Sprint 65 W3). At night the text takes the accent itself. Scoped styles take the same rule from --ink-<name>.

contrast.$comment: [Sprint 65 W3] The pairs every look must read, checked by web/scripts/tokens.mjs and mobile/tool/tokens.dart (the build fails below the ratio), at night and by day. ink:X is the accent X at night and its ink above by day; line:X is that line's badge (fg on bg). Emerald text is brandLight and red text danger (brand and live are fills). Text 4.5:1 (WCAG AA); the focus ring, icons and marks 3:1.

font.$license: Tajawal (Boutros, SIL Open Font License; X100, the owner's choice 2026-11-05, in place of Amin): four weights (400, 500, 700, 800), Arabic and Latin, served from web/public/fonts (woff2). Barlow Condensed: SIL Open Font License, from Google Fonts, for the scores and counters.

match.$homeSide: RTL: the home team sits on the right of the score bug, so the score string reads away-home left to right.

stage.$comment: [Sprint 47] The app's stage in the approved design (the owner, 2026-11-07: the web's colours with the manager games' mechanics, in place of Sprint 46's blue arena): the night ground, the navy cards, the mint accent, the top bar's pills, the green alert, the quest's gold. The same values as color (night), named for where the app uses them.

type.$comment: [Sprint 54 D1] The type scale: six roles (and display in two sizes), the only text sizes a screen may use, on the web (text-caption ... text-display-lg, scripts/tokens.mjs) and in the app (GlmType, tool/tokens.dart). caption is the smallest text allowed (W-D16: 80% of a table's text was under 12px). size in px, line as a ratio, weight as a font weight.

spacing.$comment: [Sprint 54 D1] The spacing steps for the components and the screens' layout (gaps and paddings), in px. size.space stays for what already reads it.

touch.$comment: [Sprint 54 D1] The smallest target a finger gets: 44px on the web (WCAG), 48 in the app (Android's guideline). Written in px, never in rem (W-D24).

shadow.$comment: [Sprint 54 D1] Three depths, all in the shade colour: card (a panel on the ground), raised (a menu, a popover) and overlay (a dialog). y, blur and spread in px, alpha from 0 to 1.

motion.$comment: [Sprint 54 D1] One motion system (X61): two curves (cubic-bezier control points) and three durations in ms: a press, an appearance, a number or a big change. Transform and opacity only.

broadcast.$comment: [Sprint 54 D2] The match broadcast's own colours (the 'pitch' world, always at night): the TV navy of the score bug and the studio, its inks, and the bright signals of the clips. The web reads them as --color-broadcast-* (MatchFeed.vue's styles), the app as GlmBroadcast; the clips' drawings (art.ts, clips.dart) move to them with their split (Sprints 57 and 60).

app.$comment: [X114, the owner 2026-11-22: the design is good but tiring on the eyes] The app's night only, softer than the web's: a lifted ground (less black under bright text), text and accents a step down from white and full gold, the mint and the grass less neon. mobile/tool/tokens.dart lays color over the night palette and stage over the stage; the web never reads it. Every contrast pair still passes.
